routes.label: Use the cosine law to determine the sides
Construct an altitude at the obtuse angle

question: Triangle \(ABC\) has side lengths in arithmetic progression, and the smallest side has length \(6.\) If the triangle has an angle of \(120^\circ,\) what is the area of \(ABC?\)
solution:
The \(120^\circ\) angle must face the longest side, because the other two angles sum to only \(60^\circ\). This tells us which side to use opposite the angle in the cosine law.

Let the middle side length be \(x\). Since the sides form an arithmetic progression, their lengths are
\[
6,\quad x,\quad 2x-6,
\qquad x\ge 6.
\]
The cosine law, with \(\cos120^\circ=-\tfrac12\), gives
\[
(2x-6)^2=6^2+x^2-2\cdot6\cdot x\cos120^\circ
=36+x^2+6x.
\]
Expanding and collecting terms,
\[
4x^2-24x+36=36+x^2+6x,
\qquad 3x(x-10)=0.
\]
Since \(x\ge6\), we have \(x=10\). Thus the sides are \(6,10,14\).

Using the side of length \(6\) as the base, the perpendicular height is \(10\sin60^\circ=5\sqrt3\). Here \(60^\circ\) is the supplement of the included \(120^\circ\) angle. Therefore the area is
\[
\frac12\cdot6\cdot5\sqrt3
=\boxed{15\sqrt3},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Extending a side through the \(120^\circ\) vertex creates a \(60^\circ\) angle. An altitude then produces a \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) triangle whose lengths are easy to find.

Label the vertices so that \(\angle ABC=120^\circ\), \(AB=6\), and \(BC=x\) is the middle side. The longest side is opposite \(120^\circ\), so the arithmetic progression gives \(AC=2x-6\), with \(x\ge6\).

Extend \(CB\) beyond \(B\), and let \(D\) be the foot of the perpendicular from \(A\) to this extension. Then \(\angle ABD=60^\circ\), so \(\angle BAD=30^\circ\). In right triangle \(ABD\), the side opposite \(30^\circ\) is half the hypotenuse. Thus
\[
BD=3,
\qquad AD=\sqrt{6^2-3^2}=3\sqrt3.
\]
Since \(CD=CB+BD=x+3\), the Pythagorean theorem in triangle \(ACD\) gives
\[
(2x-6)^2=(x+3)^2+27.
\]
Consequently,
\[
4x^2-24x+36=x^2+6x+36,
\qquad 3x(x-10)=0.
\]
The condition \(x\ge6\) leaves \(x=10\).

Using base \(BC\) and height \(AD\), the area is
\[
\frac12\cdot10\cdot3\sqrt3
=\boxed{15\sqrt3},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Use a 30° right triangle
